In the limit \(R>\sqrt{2}\,l\) the static electric field of the two rings provides a stable axial restoring force but a radially repulsive one.  Rotating the rings with angular speed \(\Omega\) generates a uniform axial magnetic field  

\[

so that the cyclotron frequency \(\omega_{c}=qB_{z}/m\) satisfies the Penning‑trap stability condition \(\omega_{c}^{2}>8q\beta/m\), where  

\[
\beta=\frac{Q_{0}\bigl(R^{2}-2l^{2}\bigr)}{8\pi\varepsilon_{0}(R^{2}+l^{2})^{5/2}} .
\]

Solving \(\omega_{c}^{2}=8q\beta/m\) for \(\Omega\) yields the minimum angular velocity given above.  For any \(\Omega>\Omega_{\min }\) the charged particle is confined (stable) in both the \(\hat z\) and \(\hat r\) directions.
